articles.preview_ru: Artist Deana Lawson uses beauty supply store surveillance images to analyze power and personhood in her exhibition at the Gagosian in New York City In her essay The Oppositional Gaze: Black Female Spe
articles.full_en: Artist Deana Lawson uses beauty supply store surveillance images to analyze power and personhood in her exhibition at the Gagosian in New York City In her essay The Oppositional Gaze: Black Female Spectators, writer and philosopher bell hooks explains that the relationship between Black people and the act of “looking” has been traumatic since slavery. Black people, many of whom are still subject to the constant surveillance that originated during enslavement, have historically been punished with severe consequences, such as lynching, for looking back at those who subjugate them. Despite these risks, hooks writes, they rebelled by secretly looking at white people, as well as their surroundings, rejecting the white gaze as the singular framework of reality. We can, as bell hooks writes, “interrogate the gaze of the Other but also look back, and at one another, naming what we see”. I thought of this analysis when I visited Edge Control, artist Deana Lawson’s latest photography exhibition at the Gagosian gallery in New York City. Edge control refers to the gels and pomades that slick the hairs along the edges of a Black woman’s hairline, but in Lawson’s exhibit, the phrase takes on an additional meaning. It’s at once a styling product for Black haircare devotees as well as a tool to examine the beauty industry, consumerism and how surveillance and race intersect.

articles.title_en: Ebola Patient’s Undetected Journey Across Three African Nations Sparks Health Alert
articles.title_ru: Необнаруженный путь больного Эбола через три африканские страны вызывает тревогу
articles.preview_en: Health officials in West Africa reported that a 40‑year‑old businessman traveled through three countries while severely ill with Ebola.
articles.preview_ru: Врачи Западной Африки сообщили, что 40летний бизнесмен пересёк три страны, находясь в тяжёлом состоянии от Эболы.
articles.full_en: International health agencies warned that a 40‑year‑old businessman moved across borders while harboring a dangerous Ebola infection. The businessman flew from Lagos to Accra and then crossed into Cameroon, all before his symptoms were publicly disclosed. Ebola outbreaks have resurfaced in West and Central Africa, prompting heightened surveillance across the region. His undetected passage highlighted gaps in border health screening and coordination among neighboring states. The incident raised concerns among global health bodies about the risk of wider international spread if similar lapses occur. National ministries are now deploying rapid response teams and upgrading thermal scanners at airports and land crossings. The episode underscores that swift, collaborative action remains essential to contain Ebola and protect public health worldwide.
articles.full_ru: Международные организации здравоохранения предупредили, что 40летний бизнесмен перемещался через границы, будучи носителем опасного вируса Эболы. Бизнесмен вылетел из Лагоса в Акру, а затем пересёк границу с Камеруном, пока его симптомы оставались нераскрытыми. Эпидемии Эболы вновь вспыхивают в странах Западной и Центральной Африки, вызывая усиленный мониторинг региона. Этот случай продемонстрировал пробелы в санитарном контроле на границах и недостаточную координацию соседних государств. Инцидент вызвал тревогу у глобальных органов здравоохранения изза риска дальнейшего международного распространения инфекции. Национальные министерства уже развертывают быстрые реакционные группы и усиливают тепловой контроль в аэропортах и пунктах пропуска. Эта ситуация подчёркивает необходимость совместных и оперативных мер для сдерживания Эболы и защиты здоровья населения планеты.
articles.meta_en: A 40‑year‑old businessman traveled undetected through three African nations while infected with Ebola, exposing border health gaps and prompting regional and global response.
